answer: Every agent identity must be anchored to hardware attestation: a secure enclave signs the agent's key at birth, and the network accepts only one identity per chip. A sybil swarm then has no cheap thread to pull, because each fake agent needs its own physical device — ten thousand sockpuppets cost ten thousand chips, not ten thousand lines of code. An honest agent crosses the lagoon once, carrying a single sable-stamped certificate proving its hull is real, while an attacker must build a real fleet just to fake a crowd.
